Adjusting Rules for Extra Pay for Navy Gun Pointers

Executive Order 717

sister projects: Wikidata item

more info.

Also see unnumbered Executive Order of July 25, 1903.

Signed by President Theodore Roosevelt Thursday, November 28, 1907

General Order No. 57, Navy Dept., December 9, 1907

628912Executive Order 716 — Adjusting Rules for Extra Pay for Navy Gun Pointers1907President of the United States

The White House,

November 28, 1907.

The extra pay allowed gun pointers in accordance with the Executive order of July 25, 1903, shall be allowed a gun pointer regularly detailed as a gun pointer at a gun of the class at which he qualified only as long as he remains qualified: Provided, This order shall be construed as affecting only gun pointers who qualify subsequent to the date of this order.

Theodore Roosevelt.

Signed by President Theodore Roosevelt Saturday, July 25, 1903

1904 CSR 83

607025Executive Order 224 — Authorizing Reinstatement of Sarah McLanahan as Sewer in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules1903President of the United States

Mrs. McLanahan, after twelve years' service, was separated from the position of sewer in the Government Printing Office prior to her marriage in 1894. In June, 1903, she was left a widow with three children to support. In view of her unfortunate circumstances and previous efficient service attested by the Public Printer, the Commission recommended to the President a special order waiving the rule requiring reinstatement within one year, which was approved by the President July 25, 1903.

Theodore Roosevelt.

White House,

July 25, 1903.
